attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The finite-matrix argument is conditional on a uniform second-order boundary OPE for locked Wilson collars in the actual cutoff-removal topology.
steps: Normalize collar OS data by q_delta=Nhat_delta oslash Bhat_delta so the vacuum limit is 11^* rather than an arbitrary diagonal congruence.
Decompose C^n=Ce⊕e^perp. Since the e-block is n+O(delta), PSD of q_delta is equivalent to PSD of its Schur complement for small delta.
Expanding the Schur complement gives delta PHP plus delta^2 P(K-n^{-1}Hee^*H)P. Thus PHP is the first zero-sum gate.
On ker(PHP), the first term vanishes, so the corrected K-form is the next valid obstruction; a negative value yields a finite Wilson falsifier.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: No Yang-Mills estimate yet proves the expansion for reflected hairpins or bounds the remainder uniformly through cusp/contact singularities.

assumptions: q_delta is Hermitian and has a finite-block expansion in operator norm with uniform cutoff/collar remainder.
e=n^{-1/2}(1,...,1), P=I-ee^*, and q_delta is PSD for every small delta if the OS bridge is valid.
Additive positive contacts have been eliminated by diagonal trace continuity; H,K record mixed boundary OPE data.
definitions: source object: finite locked reflected Wilson collar OS matrices N_delta with boundary Gram anomaly B_delta and diagonal normalization fixed before cutoff removal.
target object: continuum OS-positive Schwinger matrix for the same Wilson observables after removing the collar and anomaly quotient.
controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions through q_delta=Nhat_delta oslash Bhat_delta.
same-theory condition: the quotient uses only prelocked Wilson renormalizations; no boundary counterterm, algebra enlargement, or pair-dependent redefinition is allowed.

equations.label: Wilson quotient expansion
equations.valid_when: valid after nonzero boundary Gram entries, diagonal normalization, and uniform finite-block collar expansion.

equations.label: rank-one Schur complement
equations.valid_when: valid because e^*q_delta e=n+O(delta), so the vacuum rank-one direction can be eliminated.

equations.label: second-order obstruction
equations.valid_when: valid for every fixed Wilson block with the expansion above and OS positivity for all sufficiently small collars.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find a locked Wilson block and x in 1^perp∩ker(PHP) with <x,Sx><0; then q_delta has a negative quadratic form for small delta, falsifying same-theory OS passage.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Converts Wilson boundary OPE coefficients H,K into a finite OS determinant test; pure one-body renormalizations cancel, while mixed boundary terms survive in the Schur-corrected form.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Uniform rank-one tangent-cone lemma: PSD of the same-theory Wilson quotient q_delta forces PHP>=0 and S>=0 on ker(PHP); conversely, quantitative gaps plus uniform remainder make q_delta PSD. A negative S-vector is a valid falsifier.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if the RG topology cannot supply a uniform second-order collar OPE for the locked Wilson quotient matrices.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if H,K are computed on a dense Wilson core and PHP plus the corrected S-form are nonnegative with controlled higher-order null directions.
control_decision.reason: The bridge lemma is sharp enough; the remaining work is an analytic H,K computation for reflected Wilson hairpins with uniform remainders.

dependency_updates.description: Closed-cone preservation now reduces, in Wilson boundary sectors, to PSD of the Schur-corrected quotient tangent cone.
The Wilson core must be fixed before quotienting; otherwise pair-dependent boundary factors can prove positivity for a different theory.
Topology must control finite reflected Wilson quotient matrices through o(delta^2) remainders, not only fixed-collar limits.

falsifiers: falsifier: PHP has a negative zero-sum eigenvalue for a realized Wilson collar block; first-order OS positivity already fails.
falsifier: there is x in ker(PHP) with <x,P(K-n^{-1}Hee^*H)Px><0, giving a negative small-collar determinant.
falsifier: Bhat_delta has zeros or discontinuous phases, so the same-theory Hadamard quotient is not valid.
falsifier: cusp or hairpin OPE terms make R_delta non-uniform, invalidating the tangent-cone passage from RG convergence to OS positivity.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 226 made the obstruction normalization-safe and finite-dimensional: after removing the rank-one vacuum direction, the valid second-order test is S=P(K-n^{-1}Hee^*H)P on ker(PHP). One-body Wilson factors cancel; a negative S-form is a genuine mixed boundary falsifier.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute the boundary OPE H,K for three mirror Wilson hairpins sharing a reflection-plane footprint, then test PHP and the corrected S-form on zero-sum vectors.
